# Taxonomy

- [S] **Autonomy**
  · conduct: the disposition to let evidence, not incentive, govern the question
  · basis: Merton organized skepticism; Longino on independence of judgment
  · frontiers: differentiate: autonomy from funders vs. autonomy from disciplinary fashion
  - [H] **Pursuing the question that won't fund itself**  ⇄ also under: Courage
    · conduct: you commit to the problem the field considers unfashionable because the evidence, not the incentive, points there
    · basis: Merton organized skepticism; Polanyi on independent inquiry
    · frontiers: differentiate: career-risk questions vs. funding-structure-orphaned questions
    - [H] **Declining the fundable reframing that distorts the question**
      · conduct: you turn down the grant-friendly framing that would bend the inquiry away from what you actually want to know
      · basis: autonomy of inquiry; funding-shaping-of-science critique
      · frontiers: someone find this: documented refusals of distorting reframings

- [S] **Care**
  · conduct: the disposition to attend to those affected by the inquiry
  · basis: ethics of care; research-ethics traditions
  · frontiers: differentiate: care for participants vs. care for downstream users of the result
  - [H] **Crediting the unseen labor**  ⇄ also under: Justice | Honesty
    · conduct: you name the technician, student, or community whose work the result rests on in author position, not a footnote
    · basis: Fricker testimonial justice; authorship-ethics scholarship
    · frontiers: differentiate: visible co-authors vs. structurally invisible contributors
    - [H] **Co-authoring with the community whose knowledge you used**  ⇄ also under: Justice › Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks
      · conduct: you bring the source community into authorship and analysis rather than mining them for data and moving on
      · basis: Haraway situated knowledge; community-based participatory research
      · frontiers: someone find this: co-authorship with non-academic knowledge-holders
  - [H] **Protecting the vulnerable participant beyond the consent form**  ⇄ also under: Justice
    · conduct: you weigh harms the IRB checkbox doesn't cover and stop a procedure that is technically permitted but wrong
    · basis: research-ethics; Belmont principles beyond compliance
    · frontiers: differentiate: individual harm vs. collective/community harm
    - [H] **Stopping a permitted procedure that is causing distress**
      · conduct: you halt a study step that participants are tolerating but visibly suffering, even though consent technically covers it
      · basis: ethics of care; beneficence beyond compliance
      · frontiers: differentiate: acute distress vs. cumulative burden as stopping triggers

- [S] **Courage**
  · conduct: the disposition to bear cost for the sake of the inquiry
  · basis: Roberts & Wood, Intellectual Virtues
  · frontiers: differentiate: courage against the field vs. courage against one's own past self
  - [H] **Reporting null and disconfirming results**  ⇄ also under: Honesty | Rigor
    · conduct: when the data refuse your favored hypothesis, you write them up as prominently as you would a confirmation
    · basis: publication-bias / file-drawer metascience; Merton disinterestedness
    · frontiers: differentiate: nulls in confirmatory vs. exploratory designs
    - [H] **Publishing a finding that sinks your grant-renewal story**
      · conduct: you report the disconfirming result even though it weakens the narrative your next funding round depends on
      · basis: research-integrity under incentive pressure
      · frontiers: differentiate: funding cost vs. reputational cost of the null
  - [H] **Pursuing the question that won't fund itself**  ⇄ also under: Autonomy
    · conduct: you commit to the problem the field considers unfashionable because the evidence, not the incentive, points there
    · basis: Merton organized skepticism; Polanyi on independent inquiry
    · frontiers: differentiate: career-risk questions vs. funding-structure-orphaned questions
    - [H] **Continuing a line your senior collaborators have written off**
      · conduct: you keep pursuing a result your advisors and co-authors have declared a dead end, because the evidence isn't settled
      · basis: intellectual courage; hierarchy and dissent in labs
      · frontiers: differentiate: dissent within a lab vs. dissent against the field
  - [H] **Letting the anomaly redirect the program**  ⇄ also under: Openness | Humility
    · conduct: when a stray result contradicts the framework you built a career on, you follow it instead of explaining it away
    · basis: Kuhn on anomaly; Longino on accommodating dissent
    · frontiers: differentiate: anomaly from others vs. anomaly in your own replication
    - [H] **Abandoning a framework you are known for when it fails a clean test**
      · conduct: you retire the theory your reputation rests on once it loses a decisive, pre-specified test
      · basis: Kuhn paradigm-shift; intellectual courage literature
      · frontiers: differentiate: abandoning vs. publicly revising a signature framework

- [S] **Honesty**
  · conduct: the disposition not to mislead — about data, methods, or yourself
  · basis: Merton CUDOS (disinterestedness); research integrity codes
  · frontiers: differentiate: honesty toward others vs. honesty with oneself
  - [H] **Reporting null and disconfirming results**  ⇄ also under: Courage | Rigor
    · conduct: when the data refuse your favored hypothesis, you write them up as prominently as you would a confirmation
    · basis: publication-bias / file-drawer metascience; Merton disinterestedness
    · frontiers: differentiate: nulls in confirmatory vs. exploratory designs
    - [H] **Disclosing a null that undercuts your own prior published claim**
      · conduct: you flag, in the new paper, that the null reverses something you previously asserted in print
      · basis: self-correction norms; Merton disinterestedness
      · frontiers: someone find this: self-retraction-via-new-evidence cases
  - [H] **Owning the load-bearing assumption**  ⇄ also under: Humility
    · conduct: you name the single assumption your result depends on, and state what breaks if it is false, before a reviewer finds it
    · basis: Douglas on inductive risk; intellectual-humility literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: assumptions you can test now vs. assumptions you defer
    - [H] **Naming the assumption that, if false, reverses the conclusion**
      · conduct: you isolate the one premise whose failure would flip the result, and you state it explicitly in the paper
      · basis: Douglas inductive risk; sensitivity-analysis practice
      · frontiers: differentiate: load-bearing modeling vs. measurement assumptions
  - [H] **Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result**  ⇄ also under: Openness
    · conduct: you release the analysis with its dead ends and judgment calls intact, not a sanitized rerun built for the camera
    · basis: open-science reproducibility; researcher-degrees-of-freedom work
    · frontiers: differentiate: disclosing process vs. disclosing artifacts
    - [H] **Reporting the analyses you ran and discarded**  ⇄ also under: Rigor › Calibrating confidence to evidence
      · conduct: you list the specifications you tried and dropped, so readers can see the garden of forking paths you walked
      · basis: researcher-degrees-of-freedom; multiverse analysis
      · frontiers: differentiate: disclosing discarded analyses vs. reporting a full multiverse
  - [H] **Crediting the unseen labor**  ⇄ also under: Justice | Care
    · conduct: you name the technician, student, or community whose work the result rests on in author position, not a footnote
    · basis: Fricker testimonial justice; authorship-ethics scholarship
    · frontiers: differentiate: visible co-authors vs. structurally invisible contributors
    - [H] **Naming the technician in author position, not acknowledgments**  ⇄ also under: Justice › Crediting the unseen labor
      · conduct: you move the person who built the apparatus or ran the assays into authorship where their work warrants it
      · basis: authorship-ethics; CRediT contributor taxonomy
      · frontiers: differentiate: technical labor vs. interpretive labor in credit allocation
  - [H] **Calibrating confidence to evidence**  ⇄ also under: Rigor | Humility
    · conduct: your stated certainty in the abstract tracks the strength of the actual test, not the importance of the claim
    · basis: Kuhn accuracy; calibration / forecasting literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: calibration of point estimates vs. of scope conditions
    - [H] **Refusing to overclaim significance you didn't pre-specify**
      · conduct: you present a post-hoc finding as exploratory, declining to dress it in confirmatory language
      · basis: HARKing critique; confirmatory/exploratory distinction
      · frontiers: someone find this: papers that label findings exploratory at cost to impact
  - [H] **Choosing the simpler model only when it pays its way**  ⇄ also under: Rigor
    · conduct: you adopt the leaner explanation when it predicts as well, and you say so when you kept complexity only to fit data you already saw
    · basis: Kuhn simplicity; model-selection / overfitting literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: parsimony as predictive virtue vs. parsimony as honesty about overfitting
    - [H] **Admitting when complexity was added post hoc to fit observed data**
      · conduct: you disclose that an extra term was introduced after seeing the data, rather than presenting it as principled a priori
      · basis: overfitting critique; HARKing transparency
      · frontiers: someone find this: explicit disclosures of post-hoc model complexity

- [S] **Humility**
  · conduct: the disposition to track the limits of what one knows
  · basis: Baehr, The Inquiring Mind; intellectual humility literature
  · frontiers: differentiate: humility about evidence vs. humility about standing to speak
  - [H] **Owning the load-bearing assumption**  ⇄ also under: Honesty
    · conduct: you name the single assumption your result depends on, and state what breaks if it is false, before a reviewer finds it
    · basis: Douglas on inductive risk; intellectual-humility literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: assumptions you can test now vs. assumptions you defer
    - [H] **Flagging the assumption you currently cannot test**
      · conduct: you mark, as an open limit, the premise you are relying on but have no present means to check
      · basis: intellectual humility; limits-of-evidence reporting
      · frontiers: someone find this: papers that flag untestable premises as standing limits
  - [H] **Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find**  ⇄ also under: Rigor
    · conduct: you run the analysis designed to break your conclusion, not the one that flatters it
    · basis: Mayo severe testing; Popperian self-criticism
    · frontiers: differentiate: internal robustness checks vs. inviting external attack
    - [H] **Inviting an adversarial collaborator to attack the design**
      · conduct: you recruit a skeptic of your hypothesis into the study so the protocol survives a hostile reading before it runs
      · basis: adversarial collaboration literature
      · frontiers: someone find this: documented adversarial-collaboration designs
  - [H] **Calibrating confidence to evidence**  ⇄ also under: Honesty | Rigor
    · conduct: your stated certainty in the abstract tracks the strength of the actual test, not the importance of the claim
    · basis: Kuhn accuracy; calibration / forecasting literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: calibration of point estimates vs. of scope conditions
    - [H] **Stating the conditions under which you'd be wrong**
      · conduct: you specify in advance the observations that would defeat your claim, not just the ones that would support it
      · basis: Popper falsifiability; intellectual humility
      · frontiers: differentiate: defeating evidence vs. scope-limiting conditions
  - [H] **Letting the anomaly redirect the program**  ⇄ also under: Openness | Courage
    · conduct: when a stray result contradicts the framework you built a career on, you follow it instead of explaining it away
    · basis: Kuhn on anomaly; Longino on accommodating dissent
    · frontiers: differentiate: anomaly from others vs. anomaly in your own replication
    - [H] **Treating a replication failure of your own work as signal**  ⇄ also under: Rigor › Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
      · conduct: when your own result fails to replicate, you investigate it as information rather than defending the original
      · basis: replication crisis; self-correction norms
      · frontiers: differentiate: failed self-replication vs. failed independent replication

- [S] **Justice**
  · conduct: the disposition to distribute epistemic credit and burden fairly
  · basis: Fricker, epistemic injustice; Longino on social knowledge
  · frontiers: differentiate: testimonial vs. hermeneutical justice in research practice
  - [H] **Crediting the unseen labor**  ⇄ also under: Care | Honesty
    · conduct: you name the technician, student, or community whose work the result rests on in author position, not a footnote
    · basis: Fricker testimonial justice; authorship-ethics scholarship
    · frontiers: differentiate: visible co-authors vs. structurally invisible contributors
    - [H] **Naming the technician in author position, not acknowledgments**  ⇄ also under: Honesty › Crediting the unseen labor
      · conduct: you move the person who built the apparatus or ran the assays into authorship where their work warrants it
      · basis: authorship-ethics; CRediT contributor taxonomy
      · frontiers: differentiate: technical labor vs. interpretive labor in credit allocation
  - [H] **Protecting the vulnerable participant beyond the consent form**  ⇄ also under: Care
    · conduct: you weigh harms the IRB checkbox doesn't cover and stop a procedure that is technically permitted but wrong
    · basis: research-ethics; Belmont principles beyond compliance
    · frontiers: differentiate: individual harm vs. collective/community harm
    - [H] **Refusing a design that extracts from a community without return**
      · conduct: you decline a study that takes data or samples from a community and gives nothing back to them
      · basis: research-justice; data-sovereignty frameworks
      · frontiers: someone find this: refusals or redesigns on extraction grounds
  - [H] **Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks**  ⇄ also under: Openness
    · conduct: you treat practitioner and indigenous accounts as evidence to be tested, not anecdote to be displaced
    · basis: Fricker epistemic injustice; Haraway situated knowledge
    · frontiers: differentiate: admitting overlooked evidence vs. sharing back with its source
    - [H] **Co-authoring with the community whose knowledge you used**  ⇄ also under: Care › Crediting the unseen labor
      · conduct: you bring the source community into authorship and analysis rather than mining them for data and moving on
      · basis: Haraway situated knowledge; community-based participatory research
      · frontiers: someone find this: co-authorship with non-academic knowledge-holders

- [S] **Openness**
  · conduct: the disposition to make the work available to scrutiny and reuse
  · basis: Merton communism; open-science movement
  · frontiers: differentiate: openness of artifacts vs. openness of reasoning
  - [H] **Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result**  ⇄ also under: Honesty
    · conduct: you release the analysis with its dead ends and judgment calls intact, not a sanitized rerun built for the camera
    · basis: open-science reproducibility; researcher-degrees-of-freedom work
    · frontiers: differentiate: disclosing process vs. disclosing artifacts
    - [H] **Releasing raw data with the cleaning steps logged**
      · conduct: you publish the unprocessed data alongside an auditable record of every exclusion and transformation
      · basis: open-data / data-provenance standards
      · frontiers: differentiate: raw-data release vs. provenance-trail release
  - [H] **Letting the anomaly redirect the program**  ⇄ also under: Courage | Humility
    · conduct: when a stray result contradicts the framework you built a career on, you follow it instead of explaining it away
    · basis: Kuhn on anomaly; Longino on accommodating dissent
    · frontiers: differentiate: anomaly from others vs. anomaly in your own replication
    - [H] **Inviting the rival explanation into your own paper**  ⇄ also under: Rigor › Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
      · conduct: you build the strongest competing account of your data into your own discussion and test it head-to-head
      · basis: strong inference; Longino on accommodating critique
      · frontiers: differentiate: steelmanning rivals vs. formal model comparison
  - [H] **Making the work reproducible by a stranger**  ⇄ also under: Rigor
    · conduct: you write the methods so a competitor with no access to you could rebuild the result from scratch
    · basis: reproducibility / replication metascience
    · frontiers: differentiate: computational reproducibility vs. methodological replicability
    - [H] **Pre-committing to report whatever the outcome**  ⇄ also under: Rigor › Reporting null and disconfirming results
      · conduct: you register the analysis plan and the intent to publish before seeing the data, removing the option to bury a null
      · basis: pre-registration / registered-reports movement
      · frontiers: differentiate: pre-registration vs. registered report as commitment devices
    - [H] **Sharing code and environment, not just describing them**  ⇄ also under: Rigor › Making the work reproducible by a stranger
      · conduct: you ship the runnable code and a captured environment, rather than a prose description a reader must reconstruct
      · basis: containerization / reproducible-environments practice
      · frontiers: differentiate: code release vs. full environment capture
  - [H] **Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks**  ⇄ also under: Justice
    · conduct: you treat practitioner and indigenous accounts as evidence to be tested, not anecdote to be displaced
    · basis: Fricker epistemic injustice; Haraway situated knowledge
    · frontiers: differentiate: admitting overlooked evidence vs. sharing back with its source
    - [H] **Publishing in the language and venue the source community can access**
      · conduct: you make the findings reachable to the people studied, not only to the journal's paywalled readership
      · basis: knowledge-justice; open-access and translation practice
      · frontiers: someone find this: parallel community-facing publication of findings

- [S] **Rigor**
  · conduct: the disposition to subject claims to the severest available test
  · basis: Kuhn theory-choice virtues (accuracy, consistency); Mayo severe testing
  · frontiers: differentiate: rigor of measurement vs. rigor of inference
  - [H] **Reporting null and disconfirming results**  ⇄ also under: Honesty | Courage
    · conduct: when the data refuse your favored hypothesis, you write them up as prominently as you would a confirmation

    · frontiers: differentiate: internal robustness checks vs. inviting external attack
    - [H] **Running the robustness check most likely to overturn the headline**
      · conduct: you choose the stress test that would most embarrass your main claim, and report it whichever way it falls
      · basis: Mayo severe testing; robustness-analysis practice
      · frontiers: differentiate: specification robustness vs. data-perturbation robustness
    - [H] **Treating a replication failure of your own work as signal**  ⇄ also under: Humility › Letting the anomaly redirect the program
      · conduct: when your own result fails to replicate, you investigate it as information rather than defending the original
      · basis: replication crisis; self-correction norms
      · frontiers: differentiate: failed self-replication vs. failed independent replication

      · conduct: you build the strongest competing account of your data into your own discussion and test it head-to-head
      · basis: strong inference; Longino on accommodating critique
      · frontiers: differentiate: steelmanning rivals vs. formal model comparison
  - [H] **Calibrating confidence to evidence**  ⇄ also under: Honesty | Humility
    · conduct: your stated certainty in the abstract tracks the strength of the actual test, not the importance of the claim
    · basis: Kuhn accuracy; calibration / forecasting literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: calibration of point estimates vs. of scope conditions
    - [H] **Reporting the analyses you ran and discarded**  ⇄ also under: Honesty › Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result
      · conduct: you list the specifications you tried and dropped, so readers can see the garden of forking paths you walked
      · basis: researcher-degrees-of-freedom; multiverse analysis
      · frontiers: differentiate: disclosing discarded analyses vs. reporting a full multiverse
    - [H] **Widening error bars to include model uncertainty, not just sampling noise**
      · conduct: your reported uncertainty absorbs the choice of model and analyst, not only the variance within one fixed model
      · basis: model-uncertainty / ensemble-uncertainty methods
      · frontiers: differentiate: model uncertainty vs. analyst (many-analysts) uncertainty
  - [H] **Making the work reproducible by a stranger**  ⇄ also under: Openness
    · conduct: you write the methods so a competitor with no access to you could rebuild the result from scratch
    · basis: reproducibility / replication metascience
    · frontiers: differentiate: computational reproducibility vs. methodological replicability
    - [H] **Specifying every parameter a reanalysis would need**
      · conduct: you report seeds, versions, and settings so a reanalyst needs nothing from you to reproduce the numbers

      · frontiers: differentiate: parameter completeness vs. environment completeness
    - [H] **Sharing code and environment, not just describing them**  ⇄ also under: Openness › Making the work reproducible by a stranger
      · conduct: you ship the runnable code and a captured environment, rather than a prose description a reader must reconstruct
      · basis: containerization / reproducible-environments practice

    · basis: Kuhn simplicity; model-selection / overfitting literature
    · frontiers: differentiate: parsimony as predictive virtue vs. parsimony as honesty about overfitting
